question: Which entry point is used to read external data into a DataFrame?
options: spark.load
spark.read
spark.import
spark.fetch
explanation: spark.read returns a DataFrameReader, e.g. spark.read.csv(...), spark.read.json(...), spark.read.parquet(...).

question: When reading a CSV, what does the option header=True do?
options: It skips the last row of the file
It adds a header row to the output
It treats the first line as column names
It validates the file checksum
explanation: header=True tells Spark the first line contains column names, so those become the DataFrame columns instead of data.

question: What is a downside of using inferSchema=True on a large CSV file?
options: It requires an extra pass over the data, adding overhead
It always assigns every column the StringType
It permanently modifies the source file
It disables partitioning of the input
explanation: inferSchema reads the data an extra time to determine types, which is costly on large files. Providing an explicit schema avoids this pass.

question: Which read is generally fastest and carries its own schema?
options: Reading a plain text file
Reading a CSV with inferSchema
Reading a JSON file
Reading a Parquet file
explanation: Parquet is columnar and stores schema in its footer, so reads are fast and no schema inference or specification is needed.

question: What does spark.read.csv('data/*.csv') do when the path contains a wildcard?
options: It reads all matching CSV files into a single DataFrame
It reads only the first matching file
It throws an error because wildcards are unsupported
It reads the files as separate DataFrames automatically
explanation: Spark supports glob patterns and directory paths, loading all matching files together into one distributed DataFrame.
